item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E003","status":"rejected","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt does not support the climate-plan, emissions-target, vehicle-ownership, environmental-degradation, or monitoring claims in the proposed summary."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E004","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The World Bank described citizen-security challenges and proposed a national and citizen security policy under the National Program to Prevent Crime, including evidence-based prevention methods, criminal-activity information systems, and infrastructure and social-services investment in hotspot communities.","notes":["The excerpt supports these proposed policy measures but not the specific claims about drug-trafficking-linked crime, violence against women and children, or judicial and police perceptions."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E005","status":"rejected","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt concerns the Calderón-era country program and its performance, but does not support the proposed claims about public-finance modernization initiatives or procurement representing 40% of the federal budget."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The World Bank rated the prior country program's overall performance satisfactory and recorded partially achieved fiscal-policy, human-skills, health-system, housing, energy, regulatory-monitoring, and institutional outcomes; financial-sector reform, employment support, trade-cost reduction, education, social-inclusion, urban-transport, and several environmental outcomes were achieved; customs-process reform was not achieved.","notes":["The excerpt does not support a separate claim that innovation was partly achieved."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"During the prior program period, Oportunidades had 5.8 million participating families and 3 million additional participating children; Popular Health Insurance coverage increased from 27 million to more than 52 million affiliates; attendance at early-childhood-development sessions increased by 30% between 2010 and 2013; and the government reported vaccination, antiviral-stock, surveillance, and risk-communication actions related to influenza.","notes":["The excerpt supports the reported outputs and actions, but does not state that the influenza health-system outcome was only partially achieved."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The World Bank's reform diagnosis stated that Mexico's economy had grown at less than 2% annually over the preceding decade, with per-capita income about 30% of the U.S. level, and identified productivity constraints involving finance, competition, regulation, labor-market rigidities, workforce skills, innovation, and key input sectors. It also identified poverty and inequality as central reform challenges.","notes":["The excerpt supports the growth, income, productivity-constraint, poverty, and inequality claims, but not the proposed reference to weak labor-income gains."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0056-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
